cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jotham stays out of the LORD's temple, and 2 Chronicles 27:2 says so plainly. Uzziah, Judah's king before him, did go in, and leprosy broke out on his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). So the two kings share one thing, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but they part ways at the temple door.

The answer is that the people still behave corruptly. The text says it plain: "But the people still behaved corruptly." (2 Chronicles 27:2). The king is doing right and the people just keep on going their own way. I think that's a hard thing to watch, even from the palace.

The answer is towers, friends! The text says Jotham builds fortresses and towers out in the forests (2 Chronicles 27:4). He builds cities in the hill country of Judah too. Cities in the hills, fortresses and towers in the forests, and Jotham is building all of it.

The answer is that Jotham defeats them. He "…waged war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them…" (2 Chronicles 27:5). No cliffhanger here, friends. The text tells us who won, and it's Jotham.

The answer is False. After the first year the Ammonites pay again: "They paid him the same in the second and third years." (2 Chronicles 27:5). The same amount of silver, wheat and barley, three years running. That's one big delivery schedule.

The answer is that he kept his ways right before God, and the text says it outright: "So Jotham grew powerful because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God." (2 Chronicles 27:6). Builder, winner, and the reason given is how he lived before the LORD. Not a trick or a lucky break in sight, friends.
The answer is David, friends. Jotham "…was buried in the City of David." (2 Chronicles 27:9). The text says he rested with his fathers and was buried there. The city carries David's name.

The answer is True, friends. The last verse says, "And his son Ahaz reigned in his place." (2 Chronicles 27:9). The crown passes from Jotham to his son Ahaz. The story isn't over, and I won't spoil what comes next.
